issue: Does the Barton doctrine, which requires leave of the appointing court before suing a bankruptcy trustee or receiver, still apply after the trusteeship has ended?

sides.position: The Barton doctrine continues to apply after the bankruptcy trusteeship ends, because it protects court-appointed trustees from suits by disappointed litigants and preserves the ability to attract qualified trustees.
cases: In re Crown Vantage, Inc., 421 F.3d 963 (9th Cir. 2005)

sides.position: The Barton doctrine does not extend past the end of the trusteeship. Its basis is the exclusive nature of in rem jurisdiction, not a policy of protecting trustees or receivers, and court-appointed receivers already have judicial immunity.

this_court: Barton doctrine does not protect conduct after the trusteeship ends; the court rejects the policy rationale the other circuits rely on
quote: We disagree with our sister circuits that the need to protect court-appointed receivers and bankruptcy trustees is relevant to the Barton doctrine.
cite: Noel N. Chua, M.D. v. Andrew J. Ekonomou, 1 F.4th 948 (11th Cir. 2021)
